newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: AIB sees significant growth in 1996.
newsitem.headline: AIB sees significant growth in 1996.

text.p: Allied Irish Banks said on Tuesday that a 13 percent rise in pre-tax 1996 profit was due to a strong performance from all divisions and geographical areas.
It said a focus on improving customer service had resulted in significant growth in business volumes.
AIB reported pre-tax profits of 421 million Irish pounds for calendar 1996 with a 12.3 percent increase in earnings per share to 38.4 pence.
The bank said in a statement that the strength of the Irish economy led to high customer demand. Northern Ireland and Britain also benefited from an improved business environment.
Net interest income at 837.1 million pounds was 5.1 percent up on 1995 and was higher in all divisions.

The group's net interest margin at 3.54 percent has remained stablle since June 1996 and was assisted by higher credit current account balances, a strong Treasury performance and lower non-performing loans, it said.
Total loans to customers gew 14.6 percent. Geographically lending was up 19.6 percent in Ireland, 12.6 percent in Northern Ireland, and 7.1 percent in Britain.
Underlying growth in the United States was 11.1 percent.
AIB's Capital Markets division showed a 14.0 percent increase in profits to 61.2 million.
Positioning for lower interest rates in an EMU convergent environment resuled in the holding of a higher proportion of Treasury assets, it said.
